mainTopic: Is there death without sin? The refutation of רב אמי, followed by רבי יונתן's defense of ראובן and בני עלי from the charge of sin
overview: On the previous amud, רב אמי taught that there is no death without sin. The גמרא first challenges him from a ברייתא where the angels ask why משה and אהרן died, and answers that רב אמי follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says they died for their sin at the rock. A second ברייתא lists four people who died only 'בעטיו של נחש', with no sin of their own, including ישי, hinted at by the phrase 'אביגיל בת נחש'. That ברייתא turns out to follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר himself, so even he admits there is death without sin, and רב אמי is refuted. The גמרא then moves to a series of teachings by רבי יונתן, defending biblical figures who seem to have sinned. ראובן did not sin with בלהה; he only moved his father's bed to protect his mother לאה's honor, and the תנאים argue over how to read the word פחז. Next, בני עלי are defended: חפני and פנחס only delayed the women's bird-offerings. רב proves that פנחס did not sin at all, and each פסוק that seems to include him is explained away. The amud ends as the next statement in the series, about בני שמואל, begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The angels ask why אדם הראשון was punished with death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge to רב אמי from a ברייתא. The angels ask why אדם הראשון was given death, and הקדוש ברוך הוא answers that he broke an easy מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: The ministering angels said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: 'Master of the world! Why did You punish אדם הראשון with death?' He said to them: 'I gave him an easy מצוה, and he broke it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting an objection against רב אמי by quoting a ברייתא. This first part only sets up the conversation. The real attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא sounds like it agrees with רב אמי: אדם הראשון died because he sinned. This opening sets up a pattern of 'sin leads to death.' The next line will test that pattern on people who did not sin.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here and think the ברייתא supports רב אמי. This part is only the setup. The challenge comes with משה and אהרן in the next step.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: The ministering angels said
phrases.notes: מיתיבי signals a challenge from a ברייתא

phrases.english: before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world!
Why did You penalize with death
Adam the first man?
He said to them: I commanded him an easy מצוה
and he transgressed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רב אמי's statement (made on the previous amud) that there is no death without sin.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אמי's rule: אין מיתה בלא חטא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. It establishes the conversation that will lead to a case of death without sin.

steps.title: But משה and אהרן kept the whole תורה and still died
steps.stepSummary: The angels point out that משה and אהרן kept the whole תורה and still died. הקדוש ברוך הוא answers with a פסוק: 'one fate for the righteous and the wicked.' This implies that death is not always caused by sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to Him: 'But משה and אהרן kept the entire תורה, and they died!' He said to them: 'One fate comes to the righteous and to the wicked, to the good, etc.' (קהלת 9:2).
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punch of the challenge. If even perfect צדיקים like משה and אהרן died, then death can happen without sin. That contradicts רב אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels' argument assumes משה and אהרן had no sin. הקדוש ברוך הוא does not answer 'they sinned.' He answers that death is the same for everyone. That answer directly opposes רב אמי's claim that every death comes from a sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first real test of רב אמי. The answer to it will show that רב אמי's view follows one specific תנא, and that other sources disagree.

phrases.english: They said to Him: But didn't Moses and Aaron
who kept the whole Torah in its entirety, die!
He said to them: "One fate to the righteous and to the wicked,
to the good, etc."!
phrases.notes: קהלת 9:2: everyone dies, whatever they did

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁקִּיְּמוּ כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ, וּמֵתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection that step 1 set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אמי: אין מיתה בלא חטא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה and אהרן had no sin, yet they died. So there is death without sin.

steps.title: רב אמי follows the תנא who says משה and אהרן died for their sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב אמי holds like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. That תנא says even משה and אהרן died because of their sin, based on 'because you did not believe in Me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב אמי) holds like this תנא, as it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Even משה and אהרן died through their sin, as it says: 'Because you did not believe in Me.' This implies: had you believed in Me, your time to leave the world would not yet have come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אמי. It admits the ברייתא disagrees with him, but shows that another תנא agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a proof that the ברייתא is wrong. It shows there is a מחלוקת תנאים, and רב אמי sides with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The sin at מי מריבה is what caused משה and אהרן to die when they did.

keyTerms.meaning: to depart from the world (to die)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the angels' ברייתא was wrong. It is saying that רב אמי simply follows a different תנא.

phrases.english: He (רב אמי) said it like this Tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Even Moses and Aaron died through their sin,
as it says: "Because you did not believe in Me."
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:12, the episode of the rock

phrases.english: This implies: had you believed in Me —
your time would not yet have come
to depart from the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 2 by placing רב אמי on one side of a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic dispute: the speaker follows a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since משה and אהרן died, it seemed that רב אמי's rule must be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אמי follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who holds that משה and אהרן did die because of their sin.

steps.title: Four people died only because of the serpent
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge from a ברייתא: four people died only 'בעטיו של נחש,' meaning because death entered the world through the serpent, not because of any sin of their own. They are בנימין, עמרם, ישי, and כלאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Four died because of the advice of the serpent, and they are: בנימין son of יעקב, עמרם father of משה, ישי father of דוד, and כלאב son of דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second objection to רב אמי. These four people were sinless, yet they died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is stronger than the first challenge. The first challenge could be answered because some hold that משה and אהרן did sin. Here the ברייתא itself says these four died with no sin, only because of the decree of death that came from the נחש's advice to חוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the serpent's advice (the decree of death that came from it)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Four died
because of the advice of the serpent,
and these are they: Benjamin son of Jacob,
and Amram father of Moses,
and Yishai father of David,
and Kilab son of David.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אַרְבָּעָה מֵתוּ בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new and stronger challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אמי: אין מיתה בלא חטא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא names four people who died without any sin. So there is death without sin.

steps.title: ישי's sinless death is hinted in a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says all four names are known from tradition (גמרא), except ישי, who has a פסוק as a source. The פסוק calls אביגיל 'daughter of נחש.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are known from tradition, except for ישי father of דוד, about whom a פסוק explains it, as it is written: 'And אבשלום placed עמשא over the army instead of יואב. And עמשא was the son of a man named יתרא the Israelite, who came to אביגיל the daughter of נחש, sister of צרויה, mother of יואב' (שמואל ב 17:25).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains where it got its list. It brings a פסוק as the source for ישי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three of the names come from a received tradition with no verse. For ישי, the ברייתא points to a strange phrase in שמואל: אביגיל is called 'בת נחש.' The next step explains why that phrase is strange.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a received tradition (not a verse)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean 'the Talmud.' It means a tradition passed down orally.

phrases.english: And all of them are known by tradition,
except for Yishai father of David,
about whom a verse makes it explicit, as it is written:
"And Absalom placed Amasa
instead of Joab over the army,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲמָשָׂא בֶן אִישׁ וּשְׁמוֹ יִתְרָא הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי
phrases.english: and Amasa was the son of a man named Yitra the Israelite,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר בָּא אֶל אֲבִיגַיִל בַּת נָחָשׁ
phrases.english: who came to Abigail the daughter of Nahash,
sister of Zeruiah, mother of Joab."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ גְּמָרָא, לְבַר מִיִּשַׁי אֲבִי דָוִד דִּמְפָרֵשׁ בָּהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind one name in the ברייתא's list from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That ישי died without sin, only because of the נחש
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 17:25, which calls אביגיל 'בת נחש'

steps.title: Wasn't אביגיל the daughter of ישי?
steps.stepSummary: The text asks: was אביגיל really the daughter of someone named נחש? A פסוק in דברי הימים shows she was a daughter of ישי, since she is listed as a sister of ישי's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: But was she the daughter of נחש? Wasn't she the daughter of ישי, as it is written: 'And their sisters were צרויה and אביגיל' (דברי הימים א 2:16)?
steps.whatsHappening: The text points out a problem with reading 'בת נחש' literally. This sets up the creative reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since דברי הימים lists אביגיל as a sister of דוד and his brothers, her father was ישי. So 'בת נחש' cannot mean that her father's name was נחש. The question pushes us toward a non-literal reading.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so that…? (questioning a premise)

phrases.english: But was she the daughter of Nahash?
Wasn't she the daughter of Yishai,
as it is written: "And their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בַּת נָחָשׁ הֲוַאי? וַהֲלֹא בַּת יִשַׁי הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal meaning of the phrase quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of 'אביגיל בת נחש'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק shows that אביגיל's father was ישי, so 'נחש' cannot be her father's actual name.

steps.title: Daughter of the one who died because of the serpent
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'בת נחש' means 'daughter of the one who died because of the נחש.' That person is ישי, who died without any sin of his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: she was the daughter of one who died because of the advice of the serpent.
steps.whatsHappening: The text solves the puzzle by reading 'נחש' as a hint. ישי is called 'נחש' because he died only because of the serpent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the proof for ישי, so the ברייתא's challenge against רב אמי is now fully supported by a פסוק. The גמרא never answers this challenge. In steps 8–10 it identifies the ברייתא's author as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and concludes with a תיובתא against רב אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: daughter of the one who died

steps.whatToRemember: There are two challenges to רב אמי's rule that there is no death without sin. (1) משה and אהרן: answered, because רב אמי follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says they did sin. (2) Four people who died only 'בעטיו של נחש,' including ישי, as hinted by 'אביגיל בת נחש.' This second challenge is never answered. Steps 8–10 show that this ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר himself, so it refutes רב אמי (step 10).
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a strong source showing that there can be death without sin. That puts heavy pressure on רב אמי's view.

phrases.english: Rather: the daughter of one who died
because of the advice of the serpent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בַּת מִי שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 6 and completes the proof begun in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word as a hint (דרשה) instead of literally
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בת נחש' would mean that אביגיל's father was named נחש, which contradicts דברי הימים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'נחש' is a hint pointing to ישי, who died only because of the serpent, with no sin of his own.

steps.title: Who wrote the ברייתא of the four?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who authored the ברייתא about the four who died only because of the serpent. It rejects the תנא of the ministering angels, because he would have counted משה and אהרן too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the author? If you say it is the תנא who taught the conversation of the ministering angels, there is a problem: he should also have listed משה and אהרן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the author of the ברייתא is. It tries one possible author and immediately knocks him out. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the angels' תנא, משה and אהרן died without sin. If he had written this ברייתא, it would list six people, not four. So the author must be someone who holds that משה and אהרן did sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (Who is the author of this teaching?)
But there is (a problem: what about...)

phrases.english: Who is the author?
phrases.notes: Asks who wrote the ברייתא of the four

phrases.english: If you say it is the tanna of the ministering angels,
phrases.notes: The תנא who holds that משה and אהרן died without sin

phrases.english: but there are also Moshe and Aharon!
phrases.notes: They should have been on the list too

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the four-person ברייתא has been fully explained, the גמרא asks who its author is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא authored the ברייתא listing only four who died without sin?

steps.title: The author is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Since the angels' תנא does not fit, the author must be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. He holds that משה and אהרן died because of their sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the only author who fits: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that משה and אהרן died for their sin, which is why they are left off the list. Yet he still lists four people who died with no sin at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (it must be)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הִיא.
phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar?
phrases.notes: The same תנא רב אמי relied on in step 3

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by elimination.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the author.

steps.title: רב אמי is refuted
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees that there is death without sin and suffering without iniquity. So רב אמי is decisively refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: there is death without sin and suffering without iniquity. This is a refutation of רב אמי, and indeed it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion: רב אמי's view is knocked down for good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אמי had leaned on רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. But that same תנא admits that four people died with no sin. So רב אמי's rule that there is no death without sin has no support left.
steps.whatToRemember: The final position is that there IS death without sin and suffering without iniquity. רב אמי's opinion is rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: The repeated word תיובתא is not a typo. The first one states the refutation, and the second confirms it is final.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the entire debate about whether death and suffering always come from sin.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ יֵשׁ מִיתָה בְּלֹא חֵטְא
phrases.english: And learn from it: there is death without sin
phrases.notes: As shown by the four who died only because of the serpent

phrases.english: and there is suffering without iniquity,
and this refutes Rav Ami; it is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result from identifying the author in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is death without sin and suffering without iniquity. רב אמי is refuted.

steps.title: רבי יונתן says ראובן did not sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן teaches that anyone who says ראובן sinned is mistaken. The proof is the פסוק saying יעקב's sons were twelve, which shows they were all equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Anyone who says ראובן sinned is simply mistaken. The פסוק says 'And the sons of יעקב were twelve,' which teaches that they were all equal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יונתן defends ראובן and says he did not commit the sin the פסוק seems to describe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after the incident with בלהה, the תורה counts all twelve sons together. This shows that ראובן was still counted as equal to his brothers in righteousness. Someone who had committed such a sin would not be counted that way.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר רְאוּבֵן חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה,
phrases.english: Anyone who says Reuven sinned is simply mistaken,
phrases.notes: Referring to the sin with בלהה

phrases.english: as it says: 'And the sons of Yaakov were twelve'
phrases.notes: Written right after the בלהה incident

phrases.english: this teaches that they were all equal.
phrases.notes: ראובן was still equal to his brothers

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר רְאוּבֵן חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected only by theme: the sins of great ancestors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראובן did not sin with בלהה.

steps.title: What about the פסוק saying he lay with בלהה?
steps.stepSummary: If ראובן did not sin, how do we explain the פסוק that says he lay with בלהה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do I explain the פסוק 'And he lay with בלהה, his father's concubine'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן raises the obvious problem with his own view. This sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק says ראובן committed the sin outright. So the claim that he did not sin has to deal with this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain (fulfill) this פסוק?

phrases.english: But how then do I explain
phrases.notes: This is the usual way of asking about a פסוק that seems to say the opposite.

phrases.english: 'And he lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine'?
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יונתן's claim from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ראובן did not sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of the פסוק states that he lay with בלהה.

steps.title: He only moved his father's bed
steps.stepSummary: ראובן only rearranged his father's bed. The פסוק treats it as if he had lain with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that he disturbed his father's bed, and the פסוק counts it against him as if he had lain with her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן explains the פסוק. The act was moving a bed, but the תורה describes it in very harsh terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'lay with' are not meant literally. Because ראובן was so great, the תורה judges his disrespect to his father as severely as a real sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק considers it against him

phrases.english: It teaches that he rearranged his father's bed,
phrases.notes: Moving יעקב's bed out of בלהה's tent

phrases.aramaic: וּמַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ שָׁכַב עִמָּהּ.
phrases.english: and the verse counts it against him as if he lay with her.
phrases.notes: A harsh description, not a literal one

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק describes an actual sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes moving a bed, judged as harshly as a sin.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר also says ראובן was saved from sin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: ראובן was saved from that sin, and it never happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says, that צדיק was saved from that sin, and this act never came into his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings a second opinion. It agrees that ראובן did not commit the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר goes on to give his own proof and his own explanation of what ראובן actually did.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
That righteous man was saved from that sin,
phrases.notes: Referring to ראובן

phrases.english: and this act never came into his hands.
phrases.notes: He never did it

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second source that agrees with רבי יונתן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראובן did not commit the sin.

steps.title: His descendants would not curse their own ancestor
steps.stepSummary: The tribe of ראובן would later stand on הר עיבל and curse anyone who lies with his father's wife. It cannot be that ראובן himself did this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it possible that his descendants would one day stand on הר עיבל and say 'Cursed is one who lies with his father's wife,' and he himself had done this sin?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר proves his point with a rhetorical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At הר עיבל, the tribe of ראובן stood among those who announced the curses. ה׳ would not have them publicly curse their own forefather. So ראובן must not have done it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible? (rhetorical: it cannot be)
The mountain where the curses were announced

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר עָתִיד זַרְעוֹ לַעֲמוֹד עַל הַר עֵיבָל
phrases.english: Is it possible that his descendants will stand on Mount Eival
phrases.notes: The tribe of ראובן was on הר עיבל

phrases.english: and say: 'Cursed is one who lies with his father's wife'
phrases.notes: דברים 27:20

phrases.english: and he himself will have committed this sin?
phrases.notes: It cannot be

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר עָתִיד זַרְעוֹ לַעֲמוֹד עַל הַר עֵיבָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of step 14.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The curse at הר עיבל, which ראובן's descendants announced

steps.title: Again: what about the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר also has to explain the פסוק that says ראובן lay with בלהה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do I explain the פסוק 'And he lay with בלהה, his father's concubine'?
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge comes up again, this time in רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא. It sets up his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are physically repeated in the גמרא because this is a separate source facing the same question. His answer adds a new detail: why ראובן did what he did.

phrases.english: But how then do I explain
phrases.notes: Same formula as step 12

phrases.english: 'And he lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine'?
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view from the plain meaning of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's claim that ראובן did not sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of the פסוק says he lay with בלהה.

steps.title: He protested his mother's insult
steps.stepSummary: ראובן was defending his mother לאה's honor. He moved בלהה's bed so that יעקב would go to לאה's tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He demanded justice for his mother's insult. He said: If my mother's sister רחל was a rival to my mother, should my mother's sister's maidservant also be a rival to my mother? He got up and moved her bed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains what ראובן really did and why he did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After רחל died, יעקב placed his bed in בלהה's tent. בלהה had been רחל's maidservant. ראובן felt this insulted לאה, so he moved the bed. The פסוק's harsh words describe this protest, not an actual sin.

phrases.english: He protested the insult to his mother.
phrases.notes: His mother is לאה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אִם אֲחוֹת אִמִּי הָיְתָה צָרָה לְאִמִּי,
phrases.english: He said: If my mother's sister was a rival to my mother,
phrases.notes: רחל, לאה's sister

phrases.aramaic: שִׁפְחַת אֲחוֹת אִמִּי תְּהֵא צָרָה לְאִמִּי?
phrases.english: shall my mother's sister's maidservant be a rival to my mother?
phrases.notes: בלהה, רחל's maidservant

phrases.english: He got up and rearranged her bed.
phrases.notes: Moved יעקב's bed out of בלהה's tent

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 and adds ראובן's motive.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a פסוק, with the motive explained
steps.terutzMaskana: ראובן moved the bed to defend לאה's honor.

steps.title: אחרים: He moved two beds
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say ראובן disturbed two beds: one of the שכינה and one of his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: He rearranged two beds, one of the שכינה and one of his father.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion adds a detail: the act affected the שכינה too, not only יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שכינה rested in the tents of the צדיקים, so it was in יעקב's tent. Moving יעקב's bed also disturbed the place of the שכינה. That is why the act was so serious.

keyTerms.meaning: Others (a name for a certain תנא)

phrases.english: Others say: he rearranged two beds,
phrases.notes: Adds to the explanation above

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל שְׁכִינָה וְאַחַת שֶׁל אָבִיו.
phrases.english: one of the Divine Presence and one of his father.
phrases.notes: The שכינה rested in יעקב's tent

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on what ראובן did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראובן disturbed both his father's bed and the bed of the שכינה.

steps.title: Proof: read יצועי as יצועיי, 'my beds'
steps.stepSummary: יעקב's blessing says 'יצועי עלה.' The word is read as the plural 'יצועיי,' meaning two beds.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is written: 'Then you profaned it; he went up to my bed.' Do not read 'יצועי' (my bed) but 'יצועיי' (my beds).
steps.whatsHappening: אחרים bring a פסוק to support the two-beds idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב speaks for both himself and the שכינה. By reading the word as plural, we learn that two beds were disturbed: יעקב's and the שכינה's.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written
Do not read it as (a re-reading of a word)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not change the text of the תורה. It adds an extra layer of meaning by reading the word another way.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
'Then you profaned it; he went up to my bed'
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:4, יעקב's words to ראובן

phrases.english: Do not read 'my bed' but 'my beds.'
phrases.notes: Plural: יעקב's bed and the שכינה's

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the two-beds claim of step 18.
steps.whatToRemember: All the views here agree that ראובן did not actually sin with בלהה. He moved a bed, and אחרים say that act also disturbed the שכינה.

steps.title: The תנאים argue over the word פחז, and the first two read it as sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says ראובן's innocence is a dispute among תנאים. It quotes the פסוק 'פחז כמים אל תותר'. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע each read פחז as an acronym that lists ראובן's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of the תנאים. The פסוק says: 'Unstable (פחז) like water, you will not excel.' רבי אליעזר says פחז means: you were hasty, you became guilty, you acted with contempt. רבי יהושע says it means: you stepped over the law, you sinned, you acted immorally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the debate over whether ראובן sinned did not start with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. It already appears as a dispute among תנאים. The first two opinions say he did sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא splits the word פחז into its three letters, פ, ח, and ז, and makes each letter the start of a word. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע fill those letters with words of sin, so in their reading ראובן really did something wrong. This is the opposite of the view in steps 15–17 that ראובן never sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the תנאים': this matter matches an earlier dispute among the תנאים
'Unstable, hasty': the word from יעקב's blessing that is read as an acronym
You were hasty, you became guilty, you acted with contempt (רבי אליעזר)
You stepped over the law (רבי יהושע)

steps.confusionAlert: פחז is not being read for its plain meaning here. Each letter (פ־ח־ז) is treated as the first letter of a separate word. That is why each opinion gives exactly three words.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of the Tannaim.
phrases.notes: Links ראובן's innocence to an older dispute.

phrases.english: "Unstable as water, you shall not excel."
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:4, יעקב's words to ראובן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"You were hasty," "you became guilty," "you acted with contempt."
phrases.notes: Each word starts with a letter of פחז: פ for פזותה, ח for חבתה, ז for זלתה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
"You stepped over the law," "you sinned," "you acted immorally."
phrases.notes: Again the letters of פחז: פ for פסעתה, ח for חטאת, ז for זנית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the question of ראובן's innocence (steps 15–19) to an earlier dispute among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע read פחז as an acronym of sins, so ראובן did sin.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל reads פחז as ראובן's prayer and repentance
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל reads the same three letters as words about prayer and fear, so the word describes ראובן's תשובה, not his sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: You prayed, you trembled, your prayer shone forth.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא gives a positive reading of פחז. He reads it as a description of ראובן praying and being answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל uses the same letters, פ, ח, and ז, but fills them with words of prayer and fear of Heaven. The focus moves away from a sin and onto ראובן's spiritual response. This opens the side of the dispute that favors ראובן.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
"You prayed," "you trembled," "your prayer shone forth."
phrases.notes: Again the letters of פחז: פ for פיללתה, ח for חלתה, ז for זרחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing reading to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. Here פחז is about prayer, not sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פחז describes ראובן's prayer and fear, not a sin.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר המודעי reverses the letters to show ראובן escaped the sin
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says his own reading still needs רבי אלעזר המודעי's explanation. המודעי reverses the word to זחפ and reads it as: you shook, you pulled back, the sin flew away from you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: We still need המודעי. רבי אלעזר המודעי says: Turn the word around and explain it: you shook, you pulled back, the sin flew away from you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל admits his reading is not complete and points to a better one from רבי אלעזר המודעי. That reading shows even more clearly that ראובן never sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's reading talks about prayer, but it does not clearly say that the sin never happened. המודעי reads the letters backward (ז־ח־פ) and makes the sin 'fly away' from ראובן, so ראובן came close but did not sin. The ח is read like a ה (הרתעתה), which is a known exchange of similar letters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We still need': the explanation so far is not enough
The Modaite, meaning רבי אלעזר המודעי (from the town of מודיעין)
Reverse the word (read its letters backward)
The sin flew away from you

steps.confusionAlert: 'עדיין צריכין אנו למודעי' is not an attack on רבן גמליאל. It is רבן גמליאל himself saying that המודעי's reading completes his own.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said:
We still need the Modaite.
phrases.notes: His own reading still needs המודעי's explanation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i says:
Reverse the word and interpret it:
phrases.notes: Read פחז backward as ז־ח־פ.

phrases.english: "You shook," "you recoiled,"
phrases.notes: ז is for זעזעתה, and the ח is read like a ה for הרתעתה.

phrases.english: "The sin flew away from you."
phrases.notes: פ is for פרח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: עֲדַיִן צְרִיכִין אָנוּ לַמּוֹדָעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבן גמליאל's pro-ראובן reading with a clearer explanation: ראובן avoided the sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Read backward, פחז means ראובן trembled, pulled back, and the sin left him. He did not sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes clear that the pro-ראובן side matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: ראובן came close but did not commit the sin.

steps.title: רבא gives another reversed reading: ראובן held himself back from sin
steps.stepSummary: רבא (some say רבי ירמיה בר אבא) also reads the word backward. He reads it as: you remembered the punishment, you made yourself very sick, you kept away from sinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: You remembered the punishment for this act, you made yourself very sick, you kept away from sinning.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds one more backward reading of פחז. It also shows that ראובן held himself back from the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like המודעי, he reads the letters as ז־ח־פ. He adds detail on how ראובן stopped himself: he thought about the punishment and made himself suffer to break his desire. The ending, 'you kept away from sinning', says clearly that no sin took place.

keyTerms.meaning: You remembered the punishment for this act

steps.whatToRemember: The word פחז is read two ways. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע read it as sins, so ראובן did sin. רבן גמליאל, רבי אלעזר המודעי, and רבא read it as praise: ראובן prayed, trembled, and held back, so he did not sin.

phrases.english: Rava said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
"You remembered the punishment for the act,"
phrases.notes: ז is for זכרת.

phrases.english: "You made yourself very sick,"
phrases.notes: ח is for חלית.

phrases.english: "You kept away from sinning."
phrases.notes: פ is for פירשת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, וְאָמְרִי לֵהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another backward reading that supports ראובן's innocence, in the same style as המודעי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראובן thought about the punishment, made himself suffer, and did not sin.

steps.title: A memory aid listing the people defended in the next statements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן (memory list) of biblical figures: ראובן, בני עלי, בני שמואל, דוד, שלמה, and יואש. These are the people whom רבי שמואל בר נחמני will defend.
steps.simpleTranslation: ראובן. The sons of עלי. The sons of שמואל. דוד and שלמה. And יואש. This is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setup. It gives a short list so you can remember the order of the statements that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name stands for one statement in the series 'whoever says this person sinned is mistaken'. ראובן was already covered, so the series continues with בני עלי. A סימן is not an argument. It only helps the learner keep track.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of key words for the statements that follow
The sons of עלי the כהן גדול (חפני and פנחס)

steps.confusionAlert: The text here says יואש, but the matching statement later in the גמרא is about יאשיהו. Do not let the name confuse you; this is a known difference between versions of the text.

phrases.english: Reuven. The sons of Eli. The sons of Shmuel.
David and Shlomo. And Yoash. A mnemonic.
phrases.notes: The upcoming statement is about יאשיהו.

steps.triggerLanguage: רְאוּבֵן. בְּנֵי עֵלִי. בְּנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל. דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה. וְיוֹאָשׁ. סִימָן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ראובן to a full series of statements defending biblical figures.

steps.title: בני עלי did not sin, because the פסוק calls them כהנים לה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רבי יונתן, says that anyone who claims בני עלי sinned is mistaken. His proof is a פסוק that calls חפני and פנחס 'priests to God'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Whoever says the sons of עלי sinned is simply mistaken. The פסוק says: 'And the two sons of עלי were there with the ארון of God's covenant, חפני and פנחס, priests to God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first statement in the new series begins. It defends בני עלי by pointing to a פסוק that describes them in a positive way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words of ספר שמואל seem to blame בני עלי for serious sins. רבי יונתן argues that the פסוק would not call them 'כהנים לה׳' if they were truly wicked. The phrase 'אינו אלא טועה' is the fixed pattern that this whole series will repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever says this is simply mistaken
חפני and פנחס, the two sons of עלי
Priests to God, a title of honor

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the pattern for the whole series. Each figure on the list will be defended with the same 'אינו אלא טועה' formula, usually with a פסוק as proof.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
Anyone who says that the sons of Eli sinned
is nothing other than mistaken,
as it is said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְשָׁם שְׁנֵי בְנֵי עֵלִי עִם אֲרוֹן בְּרִית הָאֱלֹהִים
phrases.english: "And there were the two sons of Eli with the Ark of the covenant of God,
phrases.notes: From ספר שמואל א.

phrases.english: Chofni and Pinchas, priests to the Lord."
phrases.notes: The proof is the honored title 'כהנים לה׳'.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר בְּנֵי עֵלִי חָטְאוּ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the series announced by the סימן, beginning with בני עלי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בני עלי did not truly sin. The proof is that the פסוק calls them 'כהנים לה׳'.

steps.title: רבי יונתן follows רב and links חפני to פנחס
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן agrees with רב that פנחס did not sin. Because the פסוק links חפני to פנחס, חפני did not sin either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן holds like רב, because רב said that פנחס did not sin. The פסוק places חפני next to פנחס, so just as פנחס did not sin, חפני did not sin either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי יונתן's claim from step 25 comes from. He starts from רב's view about פנחס and extends it to חפני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב only spoke about פנחס, but רבי יונתן said that both בני עלי did not sin. He gets there with a היקש: the two brothers are mentioned together, so they share the same status.

keyTerms.meaning: He compares or links (one case to another)
Chofni, one of the two sons of עלי
Pinchas, the other son of עלי (not the Pinchas from the time of משה)

steps.confusionAlert: This פנחס is the son of עלי the כהן גדול. He is not פנחס בן אלעזר who killed זמרי.

phrases.english: He holds like Rav,
as Rav said: Pinchas did not sin.
He compares Chofni to Pinchas:
just as Pinchas did not sin,
so too Chofni did not sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis for רבי יונתן's statement in step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both חפני and פנחס did not sin. רבי יונתן builds this on רב's view about פנחס and a היקש of the two brothers.

steps.title: What about the verse saying they lay with the women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: a פסוק says the sons of עלי lay with the women.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק 'that they lay with the women'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. A פסוק in שמואל seems to say clearly that the sons of עלי committed a serious sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If neither son sinned, the פסוק that describes them lying with the women seems to contradict that. The challenge asks what this פסוק can mean.

phrases.english: But how do I explain
"that they lay with the women"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that חפני and פנחס did not sin
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that neither son of עלי sinned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly describes them lying with the women, so it seems they did sin.

steps.title: They delayed the women's bird-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The sons of עלי delayed the women's bird-offerings. Because of this, the women could not go home to their husbands, so the פסוק counts it as if the sons lay with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they delayed the women's bird-offerings, the women did not go back to their husbands. So the פסוק treats them as if they had lain with the women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק describes negligence, not a real forbidden relationship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman after childbirth brings קינים (a pair of birds) before she is fully purified. When the כהנים delayed these offerings, the women had to stay and could not return to their husbands. The פסוק uses strong language to show how serious that delay was.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird-offerings: a pair of birds brought by a woman after childbirth
The פסוק counts it against them (as if...)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a פסוק may describe a lesser wrong in harsh terms to stress how serious it is.

phrases.english: Since they delayed their bird-offerings,
so that they did not go to their husbands,
the verse counts it against them
as if they had lain with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק describes an actual forbidden relationship
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes delaying the women's offerings, which kept them from their husbands
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יונתן, the sons of עלי did not commit adultery. Their wrong was delaying the women's קינים.

steps.title: רב's proof: פנחס's grandson is named as a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now looks at רב's statement by itself. רב proves that פנחס did not sin, because a פסוק traces the כהן אחיה back to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רב said: פנחס did not sin, as it says: 'And אחיה son of אחיטוב, brother of אי כבוד, son of פנחס son of עלי, the כהן of ה׳.' Could it be that he sinned and the פסוק still lists his family line through him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's statement, which was quoted in step 26, and looks at his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק proudly lists the grandson אחיה through פנחס. רב argues that the תורה would not connect a כהן's family line to someone who committed such a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Now to the statement itself (looking directly at a statement quoted earlier)
It traces the family line through him
Is it possible...? (here a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: Now to the matter itself. Rav said:
Pinchas did not sin,
as it says: "And Achiyah son of Achituv,
brother of I-Chavod,
son of Pinchas, son of Eli,
priest of ה׳, etc."
Is it possible that sin came into his hand
and the verse traces lineage through him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to look closely at רב's statement quoted in step 26
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א יד:ג, which traces the כהן אחיה back to פנחס

steps.title: A sinner would have no descendant offering sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The proof is backed by a פסוק in מלאכי. A sinner of this kind is cut off from having scholarly descendants, or, if he is a כהן, from having a son who brings offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't it already say: 'ה׳ will cut off from the man who does this anyone awake and answering from the tents of יעקב, and anyone bringing an offering to ה׳ צבאות'? If he is a regular Jew, he will have no sharp one among the חכמים and no one who can answer among the students. If he is a כהן, he will have no son who brings a מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the family-line proof works. It uses a פסוק that says what happens to the descendants of a person who sins this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to מלאכי, a כהן who committed this sin would have no descendant serving at the מזבח. פנחס's grandson אחיה did serve as a כהן, so פנחס could not have committed this sin.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is awake (sharp) and one who answers

phrases.english: Has it not already been said:
"ה׳ will cut off from the man
who does this
one awake and one answering from the tents of Jacob
and one presenting an offering to ה׳ of hosts."
If he is an Israelite,
he will not have one who is sharp among the Sages
nor one who answers among the students.
And if he is a priest,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ בֵּן מַגִּישׁ מִנְחָה.
phrases.english: he will not have a son who presents an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the principle that makes the proof in step 29 work
steps.raayaObject: A sinning כהן would not have descendants serving as כהנים

steps.title: Conclusion: פנחס did not sin
steps.stepSummary: Rather, we can learn from this that פנחס did not sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: So, must we not learn from this that פנחס did not sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the two פסוקים together and states the conclusion of רב's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sinning כהן has no descendant bringing offerings, and פנחס did have a grandson who was a כהן. So פנחס did not sin.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not to be learned from this:
Pinchas did not sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the proof from steps 29 and 30
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פנחס did not sin, because his descendants served as כהנים.

steps.title: But the verse uses the plural 'they lay'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the פסוק says ישכבון, in the plural, which suggests that both sons, including פנחס, were involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'that they lay'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's conclusion using the grammar of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישכבון is plural, so it seems to describe both brothers together. That would put פנחס in the sin as well, against רב.

phrases.english: But it is written: "that they lay"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 31
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that פנחס did not sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural verb includes both sons, so פנחס seems to be included.

steps.title: The word is written to be read in the singular
steps.stepSummary: The word is written without a ו, so it can be read as ישכבן, meaning 'he lay', referring to only one son.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'ישכבן' (without the ו), which can be read as singular.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the spelling of the word in the תורה points to only one person, not both brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We pronounce the word as plural, but it is spelled without a ו and can be read as singular. So the פסוק does not have to include פנחס, and רב's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He lay (singular reading, spelled without a ו)
It is written (refers to the spelling, not the pronunciation)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse how a word is read aloud with how it is spelled. The answer depends on the written spelling (the כתיב), which allows a singular reading.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: פנחס did not sin. This is proven by his family line of כהנים, and the plural-sounding word is spelled so it can be read in the singular.

phrases.english: "Yishkaven" [singular] is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the grammar challenge of step 32
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verb is plural and includes both sons
steps.terutzMaskana: The spelling allows a singular reading, so the פסוק does not include פנחס

steps.title: Challenge from עלי's words 'my sons'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב again with a פסוק where עלי rebukes 'my sons' in the plural, which suggests both sons sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'No, my sons, for the report is not good'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק to attack רב's claim that פנחס did not sin. עלי speaks to 'my sons' in the plural, which sounds like both sons were guilty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל א ב:כד, עלי rebukes his children with the word בָּנָי, 'my sons.' If עלי rebuked both of them, that suggests פנחס also did wrong. This is the same kind of attack as the ישכבון challenge in Step 32, now based on a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (a formula that opens a challenge from a פסוק)
A report, a rumor that was heard

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"No, my sons,
phrases.notes: Plural form, which implies both sons

phrases.english: for the report is not good"!
phrases.notes: שמואל א ב:כד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ישכבון challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new פסוק with the same type of challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's conclusion that פנחס did not sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עלי addresses 'my sons' in the plural, which implies both sons were being rebuked for sin.

steps.title: The word is written as 'my son', singular
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is written so that it can be read as בְּנִי, 'my son,' in the singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: 'My son' (singular) is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge by pointing to how the word is spelled in the פסוק. It can be read as 'my son,' which refers to only one son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The written letters of the word (the כתיב) allow a singular reading, בְּנִי. So עלי's rebuke can be understood as aimed only at חפני. This uses the same method as Step 33: the spelling supports one sinner, not two.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (refers to the actual spelling of the word in the פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up how a word is read aloud (קרי) with how it is spelled (כתיב). The reading may sound plural, but the גמרא is drawing its lesson from the spelling, which allows a singular meaning.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
"My son" is written.
phrases.notes: The spelling allows a singular reading

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading from the spelling (כתיב) of the word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בָּנָי means both sons, so פנחס sinned too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The spelling can be read as בְּנִי, one son only, so the rebuke is aimed at חפני.

steps.title: Challenge from 'you make them transgress' in the plural
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again from the same פסוק: מַעֲבִרִים, 'you cause to transgress,' is a plural verb.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written 'מעברים' (you, plural, cause to transgress)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with the same פסוק. The verb 'you cause the people to transgress' is in the plural, which again suggests both sons sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the word 'my son' can be read in the singular, the verb later in the same פסוק looks plural. That would mean more than one son was making the people sin.

phrases.english: But isn't it written "you (plural) cause to transgress"!
phrases.notes: From the end of שמואל א ב:כד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a further plural word from the same פסוק answered in Step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The singular reading offered in Step 35, and רב's view as a whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural verb implies that multiple sons caused the people to sin.

steps.title: The verb is written in the singular
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that the word is written מַעֲבִירָם, which can be read as a singular verb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: 'מעבירם' (you, singular, cause them to transgress) is written.
steps.whatsHappening: Again the answer comes from the spelling. The word is written in a way that allows a singular reading: 'you (one person) cause them to transgress.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the spelling lacks a י, the word can be read as מַעֲבִירָם, meaning one person causes the people to sin. This keeps the whole פסוק consistent with only חפני being the sinner.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
"You cause them to transgress" (singular) is written.
phrases.notes: Written without a י, so it can be read in the singular

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading from the spelling (כתיב) of the word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural verb shows that both sons caused sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The spelling allows a singular reading, so only one son is meant.

steps.title: Challenge from 'sons of בליעל'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a final challenge: the פסוק calls עלי's sons בני בליעל, scoundrels, in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written 'בני בליעל' (scoundrels)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one last challenge. A different פסוק calls עלי's sons 'scoundrels,' which seems to include both of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל א ב:יב says 'the sons of עלי were בני בליעל.' This is harder to answer than the earlier challenges. The plural here cannot easily be removed by a spelling trick, because the פסוק clearly describes both sons.

phrases.english: But isn't it written "scoundrels"!
phrases.notes: שמואל א ב:יב, "The sons of Eli were scoundrels"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, stronger challenge from a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's conclusion that פנחס did not sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק labels both sons as בני בליעל, which implies both were sinners.

steps.title: פנחס is blamed for not protesting
steps.stepSummary: Because פנחס could have protested חפני's behavior and did not, the פסוק counts it against him as if he had sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since פנחס should have protested to חפני and did not protest, the פסוק considers it as if he sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the פסוק includes פנחס, but explains why. He did not do the sin himself. He is blamed for staying silent when he should have protested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is different from the spelling answers. It agrees that both sons are called בני בליעל, but says the label means different things for each one. חפני actually sinned, while פנחס is held responsible for failing to protest. So רב's point stands: פנחס did not commit the act.

keyTerms.meaning: To protest, to object to wrongdoing
The פסוק regards him / counts it against him

steps.whatToRemember: פנחס did not commit the sin. The פסוקים that seem to include him are explained either by their singular spelling or by the idea that someone who could protest and stays silent is treated as if he sinned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a major principle: a person who is able to stop wrongdoing and does not protest carries responsibility for it. This idea ties into the larger theme of the sugya about being held accountable for others' sins.

phrases.english: Since Pinchas should have
protested to Chofni, and he did not protest,
the verse regards him
as if he had sinned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 38 and closes the defense of פנחס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the label applies to פנחס because he failed to protest, not because he did the act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling both sons בני בליעל proves that פנחס actually sinned.
steps.terutzMaskana: פנחס is called a sinner only because he did not protest; he did not commit the act.

steps.title: New statement from רבי יונתן begins
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני begins quoting רבי יונתן with the words 'Anyone who says...', opening a new statement that continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Anyone who says...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new statement. רבי שמואל בר נחמני begins quoting רבי יונתן, and the rest of the statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening 'Anyone who says' introduces a teaching that rejects a common claim. Following the order of the סימן in step 24 (ראובן, בני עלי, בני שמואל, דוד, שלמה...), the next figures the גמרא will defend from the charge of sin are בני שמואל. It follows the same pattern as the defense of בני עלי.

keyTerms.meaning: Anyone who says (opens a statement rejecting a certain claim)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
Anyone who says
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the defense of פנחס is finished, a new statement begins in the same style.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Statement incomplete on this amud; it begins 'Anyone who says' and continues in the next section.
